tasks.//typecheck:js:deno: `typecheck:js`'s Deno step: `deno check` under the bench config over `benches/js` and `scripts`, directory arguments, not per-directory globs: deno walks them (skipping node_modules) so a new subdirectory is covered the day it appears, where a glob list silently is not; the walk takes in the Node roots too, resolving their `@fuzdev/gro` from the root install. It needs the bench install (`npm run bench:install`); docs/tasks.md §`typecheck:js` has the rest.
tasks.//typecheck:deno: The bench's Deno row's own files under Deno's checker: `benches/js/lib/ffi.ts`, the C-FFI wrapper the Deno row loads, and `scripts/pgo/ffi_ops.ts`, the driver `build:pgo`'s `--ffi` world runs under `deno`, each with what it imports. Named files rather than a walk: everything else in `scripts/` runs under Node and is typechecked by `tsc` in `typecheck:scripts`. `DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1` keeps the root package.json and the node_modules npm installs from it out of resolution, so the check needs no install and a bare import fails it; `--no-lock`: the repo is deliberately deno.lock-free. NOT in `check`, whose one Deno task is `test:deno` (cargo's `test` also runs one test with the `deno` on `PATH`): `bench:deno` runs it ahead of the Deno row and `typecheck:js` with the rest of the harness, so a kept file gone stale fails the next Deno bench, not a commit.
tasks.//branch:report: One document comparing two refs on every axis a merge read needs (sizes, type widths, work counters, recursion depth; build wall and timing behind --timing; see scripts/branch_report/branch_report.ts). Builds each ref from git in its own tree and target dir under ~/.cache/tsv/branch_report, and writes report.md + report.json. The same ref on both sides is the A/A null, whose JSON is the floor for later timing rows (--aa). A missing tool, skip or failed build is reported and exits non-zero unless --accept-gaps. NOT in `check` — it builds two release trees.
tasks.//rsvelte-allow-run: The rsvelte-fmt row spawns a prebuilt binary (it ships no in-process API — see benches/js/lib/rsvelte.ts), so `smoke` must permit it by path (a bench run's pre-flight child is granted the one installed binary by `benches/js/lib/bench_child.ts`). All five published platform packages are listed because the task string is static while the installed one is per-machine; Deno ignores a nonexistent path entry silently (unlike a bare NAME, which logs a resolution failure), so the four that don't apply cost nothing. Node and Bun need no equivalent.
tasks.//bench:deno:run: The ORCHESTRATOR's permissions only. A bench run is several processes (benches/js/bench.ts §Process model): this one loads no engine and no corpus — it starts the pre-flight process and one process per timed row per pass, and writes the report — so it asks for read, write to the results directory, and to run `deno` (its children) and `git` (the report's commit). What the children may do (FFI, the rsvelte-fmt binary, gzip, net) is stated once, in benches/js/lib/bench_child.ts, since Deno hands a child none of its parent's permissions. `--v8-flags=--expose-gc` is passed on to the children, which is where it is used.
tasks.//test:deno: The suite still on `deno test`, the one whose module under test calls `Deno.*` in the paths it tests, so it gates in `check` beside `test:node` (vitest under Node, which runs the rest; docs/tasks.md §`test:node`): `scripts/branch_report/side_test.ts`, the branch report's corpus identity over a scratch git repo — a test that spawns a process and writes, so it runs with `--allow-read --allow-write --allow-run=git`, plus `--allow-env` for exactly the three variables that point git at another repo (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`), which it clears so a run under a git hook cannot write the outer repo's index. Named paths, so a new Deno suite has to be added by name. It runs with `DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1`, so the root package.json and the node_modules npm installs from it stay out of their resolution, as in `typecheck:deno`, and a bare import still fails them; and with `--no-config`: they need nothing from the root config.
